title: Triage review of c36's condensate food chain: on fresh seed 7, prey droplets form from noise, predator droplets appear by t~400, clear prey patches and die out by t~2500, and prey reach 61 persistent splits, generation 3, merges 0.32 of splits
summary: One labkit re-run of the unchanged world on new seed 7 (256^2, t=10000, 100 frames, as the claim). Sheet t=0: smoothed noise over the whole domain. By t=400 about 200 prey droplets and many small predator droplets; predators sit on dark (fuel-depleted, prey-cleared) patches at t=900-1700 and are gone by t~2500 (species predator: final 0, max 71). Prey: 181 droplets at the end, 61 persistent splits, max generation 3, merge/split 0.32 (claim seed 0: 40 persistent, generation 3). After the predators die out the prey settle into a near-hexagonal emulsion, as in the claim.

observations.D: rerun/FACTS.md species prey: 61 persistent splits, max generation 3, merge/split 0.32
observations.X: rerun/sheet.png t=400-2200: predator droplets on prey-cleared, fuel-depleted patches; predators extinct by t~2500

seeds_run.result: pass: predation wave then prey-only emulsion; 61 persistent prey splits, gen 3

verdicts.limitation: Triage only: I did not re-run the predator-free twin, so the effect of predation on prey reproduction (X's sign) rests on the claim's pack_nopred. I did not check that the dividing prey are the ones next to cleared patches. Predation is a mass-action reaction between materials. Predators go extinct after one wave, as the claim says.
